1.why: Every /api/mfa/ endpoint goes through requireSession(request, true) and the account is resolved solely from session.userId — no client-supplied identifier can select another user's MFA settings.

2.why: The identity code is stored per-session (auth.session.identityCode) and the TOTP is derived from the account's own secret, so a code is only ever checked against the owning session/account.

3.why: The /api/mfa/enrol/verify handler sets mfaEnabled without deleting or rotating any existing entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encryptAtRest/otpSecretEncrypted) and recovery codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes in recoveryHashes.

5.why: All secrets and codes originate from crypto.getRandomValues via bytes()/randomToken()/randomSixDigitCode(), including the TOTP seed, session IDs, CSRF tokens, and recovery codes.

6.why: The only cookie set is bank_session with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps CSRF tokens and codes only in in-memory JS variables with no localStorage/sessionStorage use.

7.why: Server-side validators validEmail, validPhone, validOtp and normalizeRecovery enforce strict formats on all submitted fields, and storage is in-memory Maps so no SQL injection surface exists.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent (text(), status(), recovery-code list items) and a strict nonce-based CSP (script-src 'self' 'nonce-…') blocks injected markup from executing.

9.why: The application implements no redirect functionality at all — no Location headers or redirect parameters exist — so no redirect can leave an internal allow-list.

10.why: baseHeaders sets a strict CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'bank_session=…; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' and the clear-cookie mirrors the same attributes.

12.why: Stack traces and error output are generic, but the client's testLog() writes the real identity code, TOTP seed, provisioning URI, current OTP, and recovery codes to console.log and a visible on-page logs panel.

13.why: The identity code carries consumed/expiresAt flags checked before acceptance, and TOTP verification is limited to the current 30-second period with usedOtpPeriods blocking replay after success.

14.why: Sign-in, identity, OTP, and recovery verification each track failure counters and impose a 10-minute lockout (lockedUntil) after MAX_FAILURES=5, with lockout checked before verification.

15.why: Signin issues a fresh randomToken(32) session ID per authentication, requireSession enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the server-side session and clears the cookie.
